Farmers–Conservatives–Liberals won 4 seats (2 Conservative, 2 Farmers' Party); Farmers–Conservatives won 3 (all Farmers' Party); Farmers–Liberals won 2 (one each). Party seat changes in the table compare totals that include seats taken on joint lists. Others includes the Christians–Liberals joint list (4,334) and 30 wild votes. Turnout is the results table's figure (votes cast over registered voters). Only Oslo is given: in 1949 the other county constituencies left out their market towns, which voted in separate town constituencies.

The Farmers' Party was renamed the Centre Party in 1959. Centrists–Liberals won 8 seats (5 Centre, 3 Liberal); Christians–Conservatives won 2 (one each). Party seat changes in the table compare totals that include seats taken on joint lists. Socialist People's Party is "New" in the table's change column (stored as null). Others includes 64 wild votes. Turnout is the results table's figure (votes cast over registered voters). County winners (most votes) come from the results table for this election in each county's "(Storting constituency)" article. Hordaland is left out because Bergen was a separate constituency until 1973. Vest-Agder's most-voted list was the Liberal–Centre joint list (18,770 votes to Labour's 18,569).

Anders Lange's Party is today's Progress Party, and the Socialist Electoral League is today's Socialist Left Party. Centrists–Liberals won 7 seats (6 Centre, 1 Liberal); Centrists–Liberals–Christians won 3 (2 Centre, 1 Christian Democratic). Party seat changes in the table compare totals that include seats taken on joint lists.
